answer.evidence: The white head (rows 0-9) widens from 10 to 12 to 14 and then drops to a 2px neck at row 10. It is a flat-bottomed box that overhangs the 10px post, not an ellipse plate. Columns x=4 and x=11 show light rows 1-4, a slightly darker line at row 5 (L=202), light rows 6-7 and a shadow row at row 8 (L=113). That is a weak top band with a front-edge line, then a front face. The post below (rows 11-29) is a vertical face only. It has a dark outline row, a teal band at rows 12-13, a yellow panel with a '3' at rows 14-21 and a grey base at rows 23-28. It shows no horizontal surface of its own, so not all major parts have a top. The cap is not rounded at both edges.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style sign: a pale cap, a grey-blue body with a yellow panel and a '3'. Measured 13 visible tones per full tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and close to kiosk-a (12), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 9%, equal to bus-shelter-a and well below nothing worse than the references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark blue-grey/brown) rather than black, matching the references. Shading is about 4 steps on the body and cap, a little shallower than the 5-6 on kiosk-a and vending-a. Texture is limited to a few edge highlights and the sign glyph, with no grain. It is a thin, simple prop and sits acceptably next to the references on the primary facts, so it is not a sticker-like fail.
